transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m sorry, I’m a little nervous. I came in because I’ve been hearing voices, kind of clear, like somebody is standing right there in my little studio. They say my name, and they say things like my work is being judged. It happens even when the house is quiet and I know nobody’s there. I don’t want to sound dramatic, but it’s been bothering me.
What kind of things do the voices say about your work being judged?

They’ll say my name first sometimes, like they’re trying to get my attention… and then it’s things like, “They’re watching how you do it,” or “Your work is being judged.” Not all the time, but it feels very clear, like someone’s right there in the studio with me. I know that probably sounds strange… but that’s what I hear when everything’s quiet and nobody’s there.
Do the voices ever tell you to do something or influence what you do?

Not really like… telling me to do something, no. It’s more they say my name and make comments, like my work is being judged or watched. I guess it does make me stop and second-guess what I’m doing, but I don’t think they’re giving me orders or anything. Does that make sense?
Do you hear one voice or multiple voices when this happens?

It feels like voices… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s more than just one sometimes. They’re clear, like somebody is standing in my studio, saying my name or saying my work is being judged. When the house is quiet and nobody’s there, that’s when it really unsettles me.
Do the different voices you hear sound like they are coming from the same person or from different people?

They seem like different people, I think… not always the same one. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but they’re clear, like somebody is right there in my little studio. Sometimes it’s just my name, and sometimes it’s that thing about my work being judged. Even when the house is quiet and nobody’s there.
Are the voices you hear ever critical of you or your work?

Yes… I guess they are, in a way. I don’t want to make it sound like I’m falling apart or anything, but they’ll say my work is being judged, and it feels critical, like I’m doing something wrong. It’s clear, like somebody’s right there in my studio, even when the house is quiet and nobody’s there.
Do you ever find it hard to express your thoughts or feel like your thoughts are disjointed when these voices are present?

I’m not sure… I don’t think I’ve noticed my thoughts being disjointed exactly. It’s more that I get unsettled and I might stop what I’m saying for a second, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing you mean. Does that make sense?
Have these voices affected your ability to work or carry out your daily activities?

Um… yes, a bit. I mean, I tried to keep things going, I really did, but my aide job started getting shaky. I missed some shifts, and I mixed up care notes, and I just couldn’t keep the visits organized like I used to.

And I guess at home too… I stopped going to my walking club and those art talks at the library. I didn’t mean to isolate myself, but I ended up mostly just staying home alone. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any sudden changes in your behavior or how you're functioning over the past few weeks or months?

I… yes, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but there were a few times on client visits where I kind of stopped doing what I was supposed to be doing.

Like I’d start lining up gloves or pill cups… even little crochet scraps if I had them, making patterns instead of moving on with the care. And once or twice I’d just stand in the hallway staring, like I was waiting for some kind of signal or something. I know that probably sounds strange. I wasn’t trying to be difficult. Is that the kind of change you mean?
Do these voices and feelings of being judged happen all the time, or do they come and go?

They come and go, I think… it’s not every single minute. But it’s been going on for a while now. Maybe… about nine months?

The voices and that feeling like people are watching or judging my work, it keeps coming back. I tried to tell myself it was just stress, but it hasn’t really gone away. Is that helpful to know?
Have you had any periods where the voices and feelings of being judged completely stopped for a while?

Not completely, no… at least I don’t think so. It sort of eases up sometimes, and I can tell myself I’m just being stressed, but the voices and that feeling like my work is being watched keep coming back.

It’s been about nine months now, I guess. I’m sorry, I know that’s a long time… is that what you were asking?
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks where you didn't experience any of these voices or feelings of being judged?

I don’t think there was a full two weeks with none of it, no.

There was a time when my energy kind of dropped back down and I was sleeping more normal again, and I hoped that meant everything was settling. But… the voices and that feeling like people were judging me or tracking how I was doing my work still kept going for several weeks after that.

Maybe not as loud every moment, but it didn’t completely stop. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you ever found yourself doing things that didn't make sense or seemed unusual, like repeating movements or actions over and over?

Um… maybe a little. I don’t want it to sound like I’m being difficult or strange on purpose.

There have been times when I’m at a client visit and I sort of… stop what I’m supposed to be doing. Like I’ll start lining up gloves, or pill cups, or even little crochet scraps in patterns. It feels like I’m trying to get it “right,” I guess.

And sometimes I’ve stood in the hallway just staring, like I’m waiting for some kind of signal or something to tell me what to do next. I know that probably doesn’t make much sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you experienced any periods where these voices and feelings of being judged lasted for less than a month?

No… I mean, not that short. I wish it had just been a few weeks, but the voices and the worries about my work being watched have been going on for about nine months now.

Some days are quieter than others, so maybe I downplay it, but it hasn’t been less than a month. Is that answering it right?
Have you ever found yourself doing things that seemed strange or unusual when you were alone?

Yeah… I mean, not all the time, and I don’t think I’m trying to do anything odd.

But there have been times, even when I’m by myself at a client visit, where I’ll kind of stop what I’m supposed to be doing and start lining things up—like gloves, pill cups, little crochet scraps—making patterns with them. It feels like I’m trying to get it just right.

And sometimes I’ll just stand in the hallway staring for a bit, like I’m waiting for some kind of signal before I can move on. I know that probably sounds strange… but that’s what happens sometimes. Is that okay to say?
Have you ever found yourself doing things that seemed strange or out of character when you were with other people?

Yes… I think so. I mean, I don’t do it to be embarrassing or anything, but on client visits there have been times where I’ll sort of stop what I’m supposed to be doing.

Like I might start lining up gloves, or pill cups, or little crochet scraps in patterns, trying to make them look right. And sometimes I’ll just stand in the hallway staring for a bit, like I’m waiting for some kind of signal before I know what to do next.

I know that probably looks odd to other people. I don’t mean for it to. Is that the kind of thing you’re asking about?
Do you often find it difficult to express your thoughts in a coherent and logical manner when these voices are present?

I’m… not sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed that exactly.

I mean, sometimes I probably pause more or lose my place a little, but I can usually get out what I’m trying to say, I think. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is. If I’m not making sense right now, you can tell me.
Have you ever had a period where everything seemed to fall apart and you felt completely disconnected from reality, but it only lasted for a short time, like a few days or a week?

I don’t know… I’m not sure I’d describe it like completely disconnected from reality.

There have been times where things felt really overwhelming or confusing for a little while, but I don’t want to say it was like everything fell apart if that’s not the right way to put it. I might need you to explain what you mean by disconnected… is that okay?
Have you ever felt like you were completely disconnected from the world around you?

I don’t know if I’d say completely disconnected… maybe that sounds stronger than what I can really say.

Sometimes I feel kind of distant, like things around me don’t feel easy to take in, but I’m still there, I think. I can usually tell where I am and who I’m with. I don’t want to answer it wrong, though. Do you mean like not recognizing what’s real, or more like feeling numb and far away?
Do you often find it hard to put your thoughts into words when these voices are happening?

Maybe sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s really hard exactly. I might get stuck for a second or have to start over, especially if I’m trying to answer right when it’s happening.

I usually can still say what I mean, I think… maybe not as neatly. Does that make sense?
